questions.text:
What is the number of steps required to derive the string ((() ()) ()) for the following grammar?
[latex]S \rightarrow S S[/latex]
[latex]S \rightarrow(S)[/latex]
[latex]S \rightarrow \varepsilon[/latex]
questions.solution:
String ((()())()) has 5 pairs of brackets.

- [latex]S\rightarrow(S)[/latex]: once per pair = 5
- [latex]S\rightarrow SS[/latex]: (()())() inside the outer pair, and ()() inside the first part = 2
- [latex]S\rightarrow\varepsilon[/latex]: inside the three innermost () = 3

Total = 5 + 2 + 3 = 10

Answer: 10

questions.text:
Consider the basic block given below.
a= b + c
c =a + d
d =b + c
e =d - b
a =e + b
The minimum number of nodes and edges present in the DAG representation of the above basic block respectively are
questions.solution:
Simplify using values:
- d = b + c, e = d [latex]-[/latex] b = c (the new c), a = e + b = c + b = d

So e shares the node of c, and the last a shares the node of d.

- Leaves: b, c0, d0 (3 nodes)
- n1 = b + c0 (a), n2 = n1 + d0 (c, e), n3 = b + n2 (d, a) (3 nodes, 2 edges each)

Nodes = 6, edges = 6

Answer: 6 and 6

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are CORRECT?
1) Static allocation of all data areas by a compiler makes it impossible to implement recursion.
2) Automatic garbage collection is essential to implement recursion.
3) Dynamic allocation of activation records is essential to implement recursion.
4) Both heap and stack are essential to implement recursion.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- 1: With static allocation each function has one fixed data area, so recursive calls overwrite it [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- 2: Garbage collection is not needed for recursion [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False.
- 3: Each call needs its own activation record created at run time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- 4: A stack alone is enough; a heap is not needed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False.

Answer: 1 and 3 only

questions.text: One of the purposes of using intermediate code in compilers is to
questions.solution:
Intermediate code is machine independent. The same optimizer (and front end) can be reused with different back ends for different machines.

Answer: increase the chances of reusing the machine-independent code optimizer in other compilers

questions.text:
The minimum number of arithmetic operations required to evaluate the polynomial
[latex]P(x)=x^{5}+4x^{3}+6x+5[/latex] for a given value of x, using only one temporary variable is _____.
questions.solution:
Write [latex]P(x)=((x^2+4)\cdot x\cdot x+6)\cdot x+5[/latex]:

- t = x * x
- t = t + 4
- t = t * x
- t = t * x ([latex]x^4+4x^2[/latex])
- t = t + 6
- t = t * x ([latex]x^5+4x^3+6x[/latex])
- t = t + 5

7 operations with one temporary.

Answer: 7
